####
Using UK’s most Powerful Supercomputer for Non-Destructive Testing


##### A Case Study on Transforming Battery Cell Inspection


Year after year, batteries are becoming increasingly vital to the global economy and society, particularly in critical industries. Worldwide forecasts predict that the market will grow by approximately 10% by 2034*. At first glance, that seems like a significant opportunity. Yet scrap rates in battery cell production remain significantly high and are often exceeding 10%**, especially during the ramp-up phase. This poses both financial and environmental challenges. Optimizing yield has therefore become one of the most critical profit levers in cell manufacturing.


###### The Challenges of Scaling Battery Production and Quality Control


Despite the urgency, quality control processes are still struggling to keep pace with the rapidly scaling battery production. Traditional inspection methods are hitting a wall under the pressure of required throughput, structural complexity, and strict cost constraints.


The fundamental challenge lies in the fact that no single inspection method can comprehensively detect all potential issues and defects. For instance, non-destructive testing (NDT) solutions like inline ultrasound can quickly screen cells during production, while industrial X-ray computed tomography (CT) can identify and characterize internal defects that ultrasound might miss. Meanwhile, process data provides critical context. However, converting all this information into confident decisions at full production scale takes far more than human review or isolated analyses.


What if there was a multimodal, AI-driven inspection approach that combined industrial X-ray CT, inline ultrasound, and supercomputing-scale intelligence? Such a solution is no longer theoretical – it is already detecting battery cell defects in milliseconds and enabling precise decision-making for every cell on the production line. This innovation is powered by AI specifically designed for industrial inspection.


###### Joining Forces: Pioneering the Future of Battery Inspection


In[collaboration with Liminal Insights](https://www.bakerhughes.com/waygate-technologies/news/waygate-technologies-and-liminal-insights-announce-strategic-partnership) , Waygate Technologies is leading the development of a fused inspection architecture for lithium-ion pouch cells. Liminal’s inline ultrasound technology rapidly scans cells on the production line, flagging anomalies and outliers. Waygate Technologies’ industrial CT technology then provides high-resolution confirmation, precise localization, and detailed defect characterization for flagged cells.


The real breakthrough happens when these distinct data streams come together. Waygate Technologies leverages Isambard-AI, the United Kingdom’s most powerful AI supercomputer, located at[NCC](https://www.nccuk.com/) in Bristol and powered by thousands of NVIDIA Grace Hopper Superchips. This infrastructure provides the computational capacity necessary to train, test, and refine AI models tailored for complex, safety-critical manufacturing environments.


As an independent partner, NCC enabled the collaboration by combining advanced digital and AI capabilities with access to Isambard-AI, ensuring secure data exchange and de-risking deployment.


Image


Rather than relying on generic AI, Waygate Technologies’ engineering teams develop custom algorithms, grounded in real-world measurement data from CT, industrial ultrasound, and process streams. This approach ensures that the system operates on structured, empirical industrial evidence rather than merely interpreting images.


In a study of hundreds of cells evaluating integrated CT, ultrasound, and process data, this measurement-grounded approach demonstrated the potential to significantly outperform generic vision-language models in screening performance. For battery manufacturers, this marks a critical step toward an AI framework that avoids the pitfalls of the "black box" model, offering instead a transparent and trusted decision-support system.


###### From Defect Detection to Yield Optimization


The ultimate objective is to move beyond treating inspection as a simple pass/fail checkpoint and instead transform it into a continuous learning system. Waygate Technologies’ approach enables fully traceable, cell-level decisions, such as accepting, rescanning, inspecting, quarantining, or escalating cells, while involving human domain experts for edge cases. This level of transparency is crucial in safety-critical industries.


Over time, high-confidence CT findings refine and calibrate the inline ultrasound models. Defect patterns can be traced back to specific process conditions, enabling manufacturers to identify root causes earlier and intervene before additional defective cells are produced.


This is the true value proposition: transforming inspection into an active driver of yield optimization rather than a passive quality record.


###### From Measurement to Decision


While many companies offer inspection hardware or analytics software, Waygate Technologies combines deep CT expertise, high-speed inline ultrasound access through its partnership with Liminal, proprietary AI algorithm development, and direct access to supercomputing infrastructure. This unique combination creates a unified, measurement-based decision layer tailored specifically for battery manufacturing.


By mastering every aspect from hardware and inspection physics to shop-floor realities and AI architectures, Waygate Technologies builds solutions that are practical, explainable, and engineered for real-world factory conditions. The future of battery quality, and of advanced industrial manufacturing as a whole, will not depend on a single sensor or a standalone algorithm but on trusted intelligence that learns from every cell.
